correctness.rationale: For positive jump weight the MGF boundary forces c≥β. With x=βt and K(t)=Vt²F(x)/2, rearrangement gives c/β≥(1−1/F(x))/x; when x≥β/c this constraint is automatic. Coefficients of Hα are at most one for α≤1, so c=β is feasible, including α=1 and w=1. For α>1 the reciprocal of F at x=1−δ is o(δ) for fixed positive w, forcing c>β. At fixed α>1, writing ε=(2w/[α²(α+1)])^(1/(α−1)) and δ=εu yields the uniform compact limit u−u^α/α for the scaled excess above one. Away from x=1 the objective is O(w) uniformly, since (Hα−1)/x extends to zero. If δ/ε tends to zero the scaled excess cannot be positive in the limit; if δ→0 and δ/ε→∞ then δF(1−δ)≤δ+O(wδ^(1−α))→0 so the objective is below one. Thus all maximizers converge to u=1, giving the stated location and coefficient. For α=2 the objective in δ is w(1+3δ)/(w+2wδ+3(1−w)δ²); differentiation gives the sign of w−(1−w)(6δ+9δ²). The unique interior root moves to δ=1 at w=15/16; at and above that weight the maximum is an endpoint limit, also at w=1. Substitution yields both scale branches. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; its recorded finite checks are not the basis of the proof.
